cases.reason: Strong Denver referral for free culinary training, job-search assistance, and help overcoming employment barriers. Current intake instructions are practical; some eligibility details remain unverified.
criticalDetails: Training is free and typically lasts 4–6 weeks. The provider's statement that students can become employed in as few as 20 days is a possibility, not a placement guarantee. [Training and enrollment](https://workoptions.org/job-training/)

Attend an information session Thursdays at 10 a.m., 1895 Quebec Street, Denver. Upcoming listed exceptions include October 15, November 26, December 24, and January 1, 2027. Call 720-799-3854 or email brittany@workoptions.org. Apply in person or through the linked online application; starting instructions follow a recruiter conversation, potentially allowing a start the following Monday. [Enrollment instructions](https://workoptions.org/job-training/)

Training includes ServSafe Food Handler and Restaurant Ready credentials, individualized job matching, and assistance with identification, transportation, childcare solutions, and housing referrals. Graduates can apply for paid line-cook apprenticeships; these are selective opportunities. Follow-up includes regular contact during the first year and lifelong access to support. [Program services](https://workoptions.org/programs/)

An indexed January 2024 application lists age 18+, weekday training from 7:50 a.m.–3:30 p.m., legal-history review, lifting up to 50 pounds, and working without a mobility device for seven or more hours. This dated document cannot establish current requirements or accommodation practices. [Older application](https://workoptions.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/WO-Student-Application-Updated-JAN-2024.pdf)

The currently linked online application opened without readable content, preventing verification of its current screening questions. [Current application](https://workoptions.neonccm.com/index.php?action=application_new&section=clients_application)
openQuestions: Which requirements and daily training hours from the January 2024 application remain current, and what accommodations are available for applicants with mobility or lifting limitations?
What documents, language proficiency, or residency qualifications are currently required, and can applicants begin while staff help replace missing identification?
What is the next available start, and are any stipends or paid apprenticeship places currently available?

cases.reason: Useful combination of free individual employment coaching and a concretely priced upcoming career course, with a bilingual intake route and college-credit connections.
criticalDetails: The official stackable-credentials page advertises free career coaching open to all, including resumes, cover letters, interviews, and job-search guidance. Contact 303-539-5698 or pathways@micasaresourcecenter.org. Direct retrieval failed, but the official page's indexed text was available. [Career support](https://micasaresourcecenter.org/stackable-credentials/)

Human Resources training is advertised online September 21–November 4, 2026, Mondays and Wednesdays, 5:30–7:30 p.m., for $75. Included services are two individual coaching sessions, resume review, mock interviews, and employer-network access. [Upcoming course](https://micasaresourcecenter.org/calendar/human-resources-online/)

The course advertises up to four college credits. The stackable-credentials page identifies MSU Denver and describes three credits for HR Essentials plus one for working with career and student-services coaches. Subsequent college admission and costs are separate matters. [Credit pathway](https://micasaresourcecenter.org/stackable-credentials/)

The course's application link leads to a 2026 interest form, not immediate enrollment. Select Career and Human Resources; provide contact information and language preference. The enrollment team then contacts applicants about the next available course. The form also permits accommodation requests. [Official interest form](https://micasaresourcecenter.tfaforms.net/5061059)

The advertised $43,000–$52,000 salary range is promotional career information, not verified graduate earnings or a job guarantee. Although titled Online, the event also lists 345 S. Grove Street, Denver, as its venue. [Course listing](https://micasaresourcecenter.org/calendar/human-resources-online/)
openQuestions: Are September HR seats still available, and what age, education, work-authorization, or other admission requirements apply?
Are $75 fee waivers available, and are there additional charges for receiving the college credits?
Is the HR course entirely online despite the physical venue listing, what technology is required, and is instruction available in Spanish?

cases.reason: Concrete tuition-free Denver technology training with credentials and employment coaching. Best suited to applicants able to sustain intensive daytime attendance; conflicting education requirements need resolution for applicants without a completed diploma or GED.
criticalDetails: AI-Enabled IT Support starts October 23, 2026; applications are due October 12. Business Intelligence starts November 23, with applications due November 9. Cybersecurity applications are closed for 2026; an interest list remains available. These dates establish advertised cohorts, not guaranteed seats. [Current programs](https://activatework.org/learn/programs/)

IT Support lasts 16 weeks, Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–4 p.m., mostly online with one weekly in-person career-development day at 1777 S. Harrison Street, Denver. CompTIA A+ preparation and testing are included without charge. Required pre-work includes approximately six hours before the interview and twelve hours before training. [IT Support details](https://activatework.org/learn/programs/ai-enabled-it-support/)

Applicants must be 18+, authorized to work in the United States, proficient in English, within commuting distance, and ready for full-time training and subsequent employment. Admissions include screening, an overview, assessments, pre-work, interview, background check, and documentation; selection is competitive. [Admissions overview](https://activatework.org/learn/tuition-free-tech-training/)

Start through the Per Scholas eligibility form. ActivateWork's overview permits applicants working toward a diploma or GED, but the application and Per Scholas FAQ require a completed diploma or equivalent. Do not assume an exception. [Application](https://perscholas.org/eligibility/) and [FAQ](https://perscholas.org/faqs/)

Per Scholas's published income policy requires individual or household income below 80% of campus-area median income; military-connected applicants have a separate threshold below $200,000. Exceptions may be considered individually. The policy was reviewed through official indexed text. [Income policy](https://perscholas.org/pre-training-income-policy/)

IT Support offers career coaching through training and for twelve months after obtaining a first role. Enrolled learners may apply for an interest-free living-expense loan; this is borrowing, not a grant. [Local support](https://activatework.org/learn/programs/ai-enabled-it-support/)

Per Scholas's FAQ says attendance is unpaid, certification exams are covered, and equipment needs are assessed individually. Another official overview mentions limited need-based stipends and loaner equipment, so local availability requires confirmation. Employment assistance does not guarantee placement. [FAQ](https://perscholas.org/faqs/) and [Additional overview](https://perscholas.org/about-per-scholas/unlock-your-potential/)
openQuestions: Can Denver applicants still completing a diploma or GED enroll, despite the application requiring completion?
What background-check findings prevent admission, and what review or reconsideration process exists?
For the upcoming Denver cohorts, what loaner equipment, internet assistance, or limited stipends are available, and what living-expense loan terms apply?

cases.reason: A specific, locally accessible employment pathway for Native adults, with named staff and appointment-based intake. Detailed funding eligibility and costs are not established on the current program page.
criticalDetails: Denver Indian Center's Native Workforce Program is an adult workforce initiative funded through a U.S. Department of Labor WIOA grant. Services include career counseling, assessments, resume workshops, GED assistance, internships, and personalized job referrals. [Native Workforce Program](https://www.denverindiancenter.org/nwp)

Participation is strictly by appointment and first-come, first-served. Contact NWP@denverindiancenter.org or 303-936-2688; the page names James Woodruff and Frances Ruiz as program staff. [Program intake](https://www.denverindiancenter.org/nwp)
The service location is 4407 Morrison Road, Denver, CO 80219. [Official location](https://www.denverindiancenter.org/)

The reviewed program page does not specify fees, tribal-affiliation documentation, income thresholds, exact minimum age, enrollment documents, or current appointment availability. Grant funding alone does not establish that every service is free.
openQuestions: What Native affiliation or descent documentation, minimum age, residency, income, and employment-status requirements currently determine eligibility?
Which services and training expenses are fully funded, and are internships paid?
What is the next intake appointment, what documents should applicants bring, and what transportation or other employment supports are available?

cases.reason: Strong population-specific referral for formerly incarcerated people, combining employment preparation with broader reentry support and a verified Denver office.
criticalDetails: Second Chance Center describes employment support and career-pathway programs for formerly incarcerated people, alongside care management, housing-related services, and behavioral-health support. [Provider services](https://scccolorado.org/)

Its current calendar describes services for formerly incarcerated participants as free and lists September 2026 resume workshops, computer-skills sessions, and Saturday Employment Opportunity Lab hours. Some computer sessions explicitly require appointments. [Employment programming calendar](https://scccolorado.org/calendar/category/programming-events/)

Denver access: Second Chance Center in the City, 1391 Delaware Street, Denver, CO 80204. Published hours are Monday–Thursday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m., and Saturday, 8:30 a.m.–12:30 p.m.; Friday and Sunday closed. Call 303-537-5838, email info@scccolorado.org, or use the inquiry form. [Contact and locations](https://scccolorado.org/contact-us/)

The provider also identifies an Apprenticeship Readiness Program, but the reviewed pages do not establish its next cohort, credentials, duration, pay, or enrollment requirements. [Program reference](https://scccolorado.org/)

The public contact form provides an inquiry route; it does not establish that a new client can enroll without an appointment or referral. The reviewed calendar did not establish that every listed workshop occurs at the Denver office.
openQuestions: Can formerly incarcerated Denver residents self-refer, and what appointment, identification, release-status, or other intake requirements apply?
Which upcoming employment workshops and lab sessions take place at the Denver office, and how does a new client register?
Is Apprenticeship Readiness currently enrolling, and what schedule, credentials, employer connections, and participant compensation does it offer?

cases.reason: The SNAP employment-and-training program is relevant, but production state and Denver access pages failed to load. Available evidence supports the lead while leaving current local enrollment and service availability insufficiently verified.
criticalDetails: CDHS describes Employment First as SNAP employment and training, with eligibility requiring receipt of SNAP. Potential services include supervised job search, retention coaching, GED and English education, work-based learning, and supportive payments; offerings vary by operator. The accessible page was on a state development hostname, so it should not be treated as a fully verified production referral page. [Accessible CDHS page](https://cdhs.nxt-dev.colorado.gov/colorado-employment-first)

The CDHS page directs people to county human services or third-party partners. It describes supportive-payment requests through Colorado PEAK, MyCOBenefits, or a partner. Its payment discussion includes eligible applicants as well as recipients, leaving the scope of pre-approval assistance unclear. [Access and payment instructions](https://cdhs.nxt-dev.colorado.gov/colorado-employment-first)

An indexed public county directory lists Denver's SNAP to Success at 1200 Federal Boulevard, phone 720-944-1449, email SNAPtoSuccess@Denvergov.org. The directory's current ownership and update date were not independently established. [Indexed directory](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1wLzO2z1A_xFPO1OWzg9NZjad9LNQ-POIyQbOYwaa7us/edit)

Denver Human Services' 2025–2027 strategic roadmap describes SNAP to Success providing employment and training assistance, including an example involving training referral, car-repair support, resumes, and interview preparation. This supports local usefulness but does not establish current universal entitlements. [Official Denver roadmap](https://www.denvergov.org/files/assets/public/v/3/denver-human-services/documents/strategic-roadmap/dhs-strategic-roadmap-2025-2027.pdf)

The supplied state URL, alternative production state URLs, and Denver's SNAPtoSuccess URL could not be retrieved. The 24 source-page-open ceiling prevented further document inspection. Current Denver orientation procedures, costs, funding limits, and appointment availability remain unverified. [Denver access URL attempted](https://www.denvergov.org/SNAPtoSuccess)
